We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =1+{x}^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =2x \\ \text{d}u & =2x\,\text{d}x \\ 2\,\text{d}u & =4x\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=1+{x}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & 2 \\ u & 1 & 5\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{(1+{x}^{2})}\cdot 4x\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{1}{u}\cdot 2\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{1}{u}\cdot 2\,\text{d}u & =2{\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(u){|}_{1}^{5} \\  & =2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$
